h1: The 6 Best Ring Alternatives of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six video doorbell alternatives to Ring from Tapo, eufy, Reolink, Blink and more, compared on power, resolution and price.
summary: The Tapo 2K Wireless Smart Video Doorbell with Chime is our all-around pick, with 2K video and battery power in the $25 to $50 range. The eufy E340 is the battery pick for those who will spend a bit more, and the Reolink PoE is the one for people who can run an Ethernet cable. The BOIFUN is the budget option that states no subscription is required.
intro: The usual mistake when leaving Ring is to compare camera resolution and ignore how the doorbell is powered. A battery model is easy to install but needs recharging, while a wired or PoE model never does but needs the right wiring at your door.

We reviewed six video doorbells from other brands and ranked them on resolution, power type, price bucket and what each listing actually promises. We left Ring's own models out, since the point is an alternative.

products.name: Tapo 2K Wireless Smart Video Doorbell w/Chime
products.verdict: 2K video, battery power and a chime at a low price.
products.description:
The Tapo 2K Wireless Smart Video Doorbell is a battery-powered, wireless 2K model that comes with a chime. Its price range is $25 to $50.

It ranks first because it matches the resolution of pricier models while staying in the cheapest bucket and including a chime. The eufy below it lists the same 2K but costs more.

It suits renters and anyone without doorbell wiring. The caveat is that battery models need recharging, which the listing does not detail.

products.name: eufy Security Video Doorbell E340
products.verdict: A 2K battery doorbell from a security-focused brand.
products.description:
The eufy Security Video Doorbell E340 is a battery-powered 2K model in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It ranks second because it offers 2K video like the Tapo but costs more, so the extra spend has to be justified by the brand. That is the tradeoff against the pick above.

It suits buyers who prefer the eufy ecosystem. The caveat is that the listing data gives no extra features beyond 2K and battery power.

products.name: REOLINK Video Doorbell PoE 2K Wired Outdoor Security Camera with
products.verdict: A 2K doorbell powered over Ethernet, so no battery to charge.
products.description:
The REOLINK Video Doorbell PoE is a wired 2K outdoor camera powered over Ethernet, in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It ranks third because PoE removes battery charging entirely but demands an Ethernet run to the door. That is a real installation tradeoff against the wireless picks above.

It suits homeowners who can run cable. The caveat is that renters will find it hard to install.
products.skipIf: You rent or cannot run cable.

products.name: aosu 5MP Ultra HD Wireless & Wired Video Doorbell Camera
products.verdict: A 5MP doorbell that works wired or wireless.
products.description:
The aosu 5MP Ultra HD Video Doorbell Camera supports both wireless and wired setups and sits above the budget picks on price.

The flexible install is what puts it fourth, while the Tapo above delivers 2K for much less. The 5MP figure is higher on paper but the listing gives little else.

It suits buyers undecided on wiring. The caveat is the higher bucket for limited stated features.

products.name: Blink Video Doorbell - Head-to-toe HD view
products.verdict: An HD doorbell with a head-to-toe view, wired or battery.
products.description:
The Blink Video Doorbell has a head-to-toe HD view and can run wired or on battery. Its price range is $25 to $50.

It ranks fifth because it is HD where the Tapo and BOIFUN list 2K. What it offers is a taller field of view and a known name at a low price.

It suits buyers wanting a simple, inexpensive doorbell. The caveat is lower resolution than the 2K picks.

products.name: BOIFUN Video Doorbell Camera Wireless - No Subscription Required
products.verdict: A 2K battery doorbell that says no subscription is required.
products.description:
The BOIFUN Video Doorbell Camera is a wireless, battery-powered 2K model, and its title states no subscription is required. Its price range is $25 to $50.

It ranks last of the six because it is the lesser-known brand, though the specs match the Tapo above. The no-subscription claim is its main hook.

It suits shoppers who dislike monthly fees. The caveat is that the claim comes from the listing title, so confirm what features need a plan.

whatMatters.detail: A battery doorbell is easy to mount but needs recharging. A wired or PoE one never needs charging but needs cable. Check the power line in the title or specs.
2K shows more detail than plain HD. It helps for faces and package labels. Look for 2K or MP in the title.
Some doorbells lock features behind a monthly plan. Only the BOIFUN states none is required. Read the listing for what is included.
A chime sounds indoors when someone rings. The Tapo lists one. Check whether yours is included or sold separately.
Wireless suits renters, PoE suits homeowners. The aosu and Blink list more than one power option, which helps if you are unsure.

faq.q: Will these work with my existing chime?
faq.a: The listings we reviewed do not say. Only the Tapo lists its own chime, so check compatibility on the product page.
Ignoring power. A battery doorbell needs recharging, so confirm you are comfortable with that.
2K gives more detail, and the Tapo shows it need not cost much. Blink's HD is fine for simple use.

faq.q: How do I install the Reolink?
faq.a: It needs an Ethernet cable run to the door for PoE power. If you cannot do that, choose a battery model.
Only the BOIFUN title states none is required. The others do not say, so check what cloud features cost.

faq.q: Can I use two power modes?
faq.a: The aosu and Blink list wired and wireless or battery options. Confirm the mode in the setup guide.

finalTake: The Tapo 2K Wireless Smart Video Doorbell is the best Ring alternative for most people. The eufy E340 and the Reolink PoE suit buyers who will pay more for a brand or a wired install. Pick power first and resolution second.
